Shakescape is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. Noncommercial use, study, modification, and redistribution are allowed under the license. Commercial use requires separate written permission from Denuo Web, LLC.

This is an experimental Handshake-first browser with local HNS proofs, authoritative DNS, DNSSEC/DANE diagnostics, and a device-local HNS wallet. The wallet\'s direct mode can receive and send HNS and manage names through wallet-owned verified Handshake peers; it does not require a loopback node, hosted indexer, or Denuo relay to establish HNS chain or spending authority. While unlocked in the wallet screen, a direct wallet can host or pair an exact Denuo peer endpoint and replicate its locally verified board without a marketplace relay. A connected board peer is transport only, never authority or a settlement receipt. Complete atomic Shakedex settlement, Internet/NAT reachability, and HNSA/HNSR service roles remain under development. HNS resolution, validation, sync, transaction broadcast, name operations, and marketplace workflows can fail, be delayed, require later manual actions, or remain incomplete. Review every native approval, recipient, amount, fee limit, name, listing, and session before approving it. HNS WebPKI fallback is prohibited; recovery DNS answers never bypass local DNSSEC, TLSA, or DANE validation. Website-provider wallet access is not enabled by these native controls. The requester-only P2P DNS relay is separate from HNSR and does not make this device an endpoint or output node. The app is provided without warranty, is not a financial service, and donations are optional and unlock no features.

Shakescape does not include ads, analytics SDKs, or developer-operated accounts. It stores browsing history, cookies, website data, download records, settings, diagnostics, HNS sync/cache data, a user-configured recovery DoH URL, manually added relay-peer IP endpoints, and a network-scoped encrypted wallet database with an Android Keystore-wrapped database key locally on the device. A newly generated recovery phrase is shown once; save it offline before confirming because the app cannot show or recover it later. If the protected recovery screen closes before confirmation, the app wipes the unconfirmed database-key buffer and deletes the incomplete wallet database. An unlocked confirmed wallet can be deleted after two destructive confirmations showing its exact network and account and requiring DELETE. The app deletes the Keystore wrapping key before encrypted database files; partial cleanup stays blocked for retry. Deletion affects only this device-local wallet and does not delete a recovery phrase or backup saved elsewhere. In direct HNS mode, the native wallet obtains peers from Handshake DNS seeds and peer gossip, verifies headers, relevant blocks, wallet UTXOs, and name proofs locally, and broadcasts approved HNS transactions through its connected peer set. Public addresses, transactions, and name operations can therefore be disclosed to the peers that relay them. A direct Denuo pairing endpoint is explicit and may disclose its IP address, port, timing, and board protocol messages to the paired wallet; listings remain locally validated against HNS state and direct write observations are not peer acceptance receipts. The wallet database, recovery phrase, private keys, database key, and Android Keystore material are not sent to Denuo Web, websites, or any peer. Browser functions separately send requests to websites you visit, HNS peers, DNS seeds, authoritative nameservers, proof-bootstrapped or RFC 9461-discovered authoritative DoH endpoints, the optional HNS P2P relay, validating ICANN DoH, WebView Safe Browsing services when supported by the installed WebView provider, and the non-routable 192.0.2.1 TEST-NET DNS sentinel after delegated DNS failure. A selected DNS relay or recovery operator can observe requested qnames, qtypes, timing, and the connection source address. Relay and recovery answers still undergo local DNSSEC, TLSA, and DANE validation; bogus DNSSEC and stale or missing HNS proofs fail closed. Browser data can be cleared from Settings, and Android system settings can clear all app data.
